items.title: Joe Wilder Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I met Joe Williams, incidentally the first time I worked with Joe Williams, he was the vocalist with Lionel Hampton’s band.

ctx.x: Was Joe Williams on the band at that time? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

No, Joe wasn’t on the band at that time. I met Joe Williams, incidentally the first time I worked with Joe Williams, he was the vocalist with Lionel Hampton’s band. He sang in Lionel Hampton’s band. No blues, he was a ballad singer, and a good one. He sang ballads, beautiful singer. And when he started with the blues in Basie’s band, I was surprised you know, because I knew him as a ballad singer and a really good ballad singer. He still does for that matter.
All of a sudden he’s like the blues man.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When we got up there, Joe Williams – he was a good ballplayer too.

ctx.x: Did any of the bands you were with have baseball teams?

Basie had a baseball team. We used to play ball. Harry James had a team. He was a baseball fanatic. We used to play even in Les Hite’s band. We didn’t have an organized time. We liked to play ball, and sometimes you’d meet another band on the road, and they’d say, let’s have a scrub game. They’d have a baseball game. Cab [Calloway] had a pretty good team. He was a guy – he didn’t like to lose. So most of his guys gave up after a while, because if they lost, they were in trouble. But it was a lot of fun. I…
Oh, no, you had to watch it.
